To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we give the first polylogarithmic approximability result for EDP in moderately connected graphs, i.e. graphs with large global min-cut.
we provide the first constant approximation algorithm for the edge disjoint paths problem in graphs with moderate connectivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a natural generalization of the classic EDP problem to a wide class of moderately connected graphs.
the following question: How much structure is needed for polylogarithmic approximability of EDP in undirected graphs?
the following questions: (1) Can we extend the known approximation algorithms for EDP to a wider range of graphs?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
polylogarithmic approximations are possible in graphs of moderate connectivity, and that this is the best one can hope for in general.
EDP can be approximated within polylogarithmic factor in all graphs that have a moderately high minimum cut, or a high number of short disjoint paths.
the undirected E-D-P problem can be approximated to within polylogarithmic factor in any moderately connected graph.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the undirected E-D-P problem is approximable within polylogarithmic factor in moderately connected graphs.
the EDP problem is hard to approximate on graphs with large diameter, but can be approximated well on graphs that exclude large minors.
the EDP problem can be approximated well in graphs that are not sparse, not planar, but have a moderate degree of connectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EDP problem in moderately connected graphs is not as difficult to approximate as previously thought.
the EDP problem is easier to approximate in graphs with high connectivity.
graphs that are not too far from being expanders are also easy for the EDP problem.
